title.narrative: WFP/FAO Resilience of farmers in Grand Kasai
WFP/FAO resiliens hos jordbrukare i Grand Kasai

description.narrative:
Den intervention som presenteras syftar till att stödja WFP och FAO och deras gemensamma program Strengthening the resilience and sustainable livelihood systems of smallholder in Kasai and Kasai Central provinces in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).
Det övergripande målet med projektet är att göra det möjligt för småbrukare i Kasai och Kasai Central att utveckla motståndskraftiga försörjningsmöjligheter genom jordbruksproduktion. Det gemensamma FAO-WFP-projektet kommer att anslå medel för att uppnå följande resultat:
1) Projektmottagarna grupperas i samhällsbaserade organisationer som är lagligt etablerade och utrustade för att tillhandahålla tjänster till sina medlemmar. 2) Småbrukare har stärkt sin kapacitet för hållbar och näringskänslig jordbruksproduktion (i kvantitet och kvalitet) och livsmedelsbearbetning. 3) Stärkta försörjningsmöjligheter för utsatta samhällen och hushåll, särskilt hushåll med kvinnligt huvud, genom ökad tillgång till krediter, förbättrat marknadstillträde och inkomstdiversifiering. 4) Stödmottagande samhällen mobiliseras för att vidta åtgärder för konfliktbegränsning och främjande av social sammanhållning, jämställdhet, fred och försoning.

The intervention presented is aimed at supporting WFP and FAO and their joint programme Strengthening the resilience and sustainable livelihood systems of smallholder farmers in Kasai and Kasai Central provinces in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).
The overall goal of the project is to enable smallholder farmers in Kasai and Kasai Central to develop resilient livelihoods through agricultural production. The joint FAO-WFP project will allocate the funding towards the achievement of the following results:
1) The project beneficiaries are grouped into community-based organizations which are legally established and equipped to provide services to their members. 2) Smallholder farmers have strengthened their capacities for sustainable and nutrition sensitive agricultural production (in quantity and quality) and food processing. 3) Strengthened livelihoods of vulnerable communities and households, particularly female headed households, through increased access to credit, improved market access and income diversification. 4) Beneficiary communities are mobilized to take action for conflict mitigation and the promotion of social cohesion, gender equality, peace and reconciliation.

The main objective of the proposed intervention is to create development opportunities for the population of the Kasai and Kasai Central, by supporting the strengthening and expansion of the agriculture value chain. The programme intends to intervene at community level to enhance resilience especially in rural areas.
Investing in human capital and in rural assets, is part of the intervention, as well as supporting the creation of income generation opportunities, and enhancing capacity of local communities to bear shocks and to manage dialogue within a context of consolidation of peace. The specific project objectives include:
1. Food security and nutrition are improved while community resilience is strengthened.
2. The agricultural production of smallholder farmers and their financial capacities are strengthened, and markets revitalized, in order to support resilient livelihoods and increase income.
3. Community organizations are reinforced through activities that contribute to social cohesion, gender equality, peace and reconciliation.

title.narrative: Decision on Contribution (WFP-FAO) in Grand Kasai

description.narrative:
This report covers activities implemented in FY2025 of the joint WFPFAO resilience programme in Kasaï and Kasaï Central, operating within a HumanitarianDevelopmentPeace (HDP) Nexus context with food insecurity, problem of accessibility mainly during the rainy season due to weak infrastructure, climate variability, localized tensions and limited access to basic services.
In 2025, Activities remained operational in 7 health areas throughout the reporting period of Luiza (Tutante, Kamayi, Mukungu, Kabuanga, Kandakanda, Kapanga and Bambaie) and two health areas of Tshikaji (Nkonko 1 and Saints Martyrs) in Kasaï Central, as well as in Kamonia Territory in Kasaï (Kamuesha, Katalayi, Mukambu, Muila Mbumba and Mukwadjanga). The main agricultural input package reached approximately 9,000 beneficiary households, including 5,000 in Kasaï Central and 4,000 in Kasaï, with one Kasaï-specific report indicating 4,032 direct beneficiary households.
Under Outcome 1, institutional strengthening of farmers organizations continued. In Kasaï Central, 44 unions of farmers organizations and 9 agricultural cooperatives underwent structuring and legalization processes. In Kasaï, 53 cooperatives and 6 unions of cooperatives received legal and management support. Additionally, 130 cooperative and union members, including 58 women, were trained in governance, administrative and financial management, and OHADA cooperative regulations. The programme also established 200 Dimitra Clubs across both provinces, supporting community dialogue, mediation, access to land and water, erosion control, infrastructure rehabilitation and sanitation initiatives.
Under Outcome 2, climate-resilient and nutrition-sensitive agricultural production was strengthened. Ten farmers organizations received 400 kg of cowpea R1 seed and 180 kg of groundnut R1 seed, resulting in the production of 2,269 kg of R2 seed (1,939 kg of cowpea and 330 kg of groundnut). Across both provinces, 7,520 households cultivated 3,551.8 hectares during Season 2025A, producing 3,196.2 metric tons of maize and 705.2 metric tons of cowpea, for a total production of 3,901.4 metric tons. This represents an average production of approximately 518 kg per cultivating household. However, only 84 percent of supported households cultivated fields due to climatic challenges, including the premature end of rainfall.
Nutrition-sensitive interventions targeted 500 households in Tshikaji with vegetable seeds, tools and small livestock. Support included inputs for tomato, red onion, carrot, Chinese cabbage, eggplant and okra production, 40 MUAC tapes for community health workers, and the distribution of 1,000 rabbits to 500 households, alongside demonstration hutches in Nkonko 1 and Saints Martyrs. Behaviour change communication was reinforced through 40 radio programmes, 140 radio spots and 6 micro-programmes broadcast over 20 weeks.
Under Outcome 3, livelihood diversification and financial inclusion activities expanded. A total of 1,000 literacy learners (876 women and 124 men) were enrolled across 26 literacy centres in Luiza and Tshikaji. Furthermore, 1,500 participants (1,200 in Luiza and 300 in Tshikaji) received training on income-generating activities, while bread-making and soap-making kits were distributed to support economic reintegration and womens empowerment. Across both provinces, 200 Village Savings and Loan Associations (VSLAs) were established and functioning. Market-support infrastructure included the installation of 20 mixed maize-cassava mills, 570 small grinders and 285 manual maize shellers. In addition, 20 management committee members were trained in the operation, maintenance and economic management of these facilities.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
